chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who commits an offense outside the Sacred Sanctuary and then seeks refuge in the Sanctuary, he said:

“The legal punishment is not carried out on him, and he is not to be given food, nor drink, nor spoken to, nor engaged in trade. For if that is done to him, he will soon leave, and then the legal punishment will be carried out on him. But if he commits an offense in the Sacred Sanctuary, the legal punishment is carried out on him in the Sanctuary, for he did not regard the Sanctuary as having sanctity.”

key_terms.لَا يُبَايَعُ: he is not to be traded with or engaged in commerce
key_terms.يَلْجَأُ إِلَى ٱلْحَرَمِ: seeks refuge in the Sacred Sanctuary
key_terms.ٱلْحَرَمِ: the Sacred Sanctuary, the inviolable sacred precinct

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who commits a crime outside al-Ḥaram and then seeks refuge inside it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about one who commits a crime outside al-Ḥaram and then takes refuge within it. The hadd punishment is not executed inside the Sanctuary in that case, but social and economic pressure may be applied until he leaves; however, if the offense itself is committed within al-Ḥaram, the punishment is carried out there because he violated its sanctity.
